sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: RAGFlow is an open-source retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) engine with agent capabilities. It reads complex documents like PDFs, Word files, slides, spreadsheets and scans, splits them into searchable chunks, and answers questions about them with traceable citations.
sixtySeconds.problem: Chatbots that answer from your documents often give vague or made-up answers, especially with messy file formats. RAGFlow focuses on deep document understanding and grounded citations, so you can see exactly where each answer came from.
whoFor: Teams building question answering over company documents
Developers who need RAG with citations through an API
Organisations with complex files like scanned PDFs and spreadsheets
Businesses wanting a self-hosted knowledge assistant
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when document parsing quality and citations matter. It's a full server with several services, so it needs a reasonably sized machine.
requirements: 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM and 50 GB disk recommended to start
An LLM, embedding model and reranker (API or local)

overview: RAGFlow extracts knowledge from unstructured data with complicated formats using deep document understanding, and uses template-based chunking that you can inspect and adjust. Answers come with key references and traceable citations.

Version 1.0.0 was released on 2026-11-06. Recent additions include agentic retrieval with Low, Medium, High and Ultra thinking modes, Knowledge Compilation that turns documents into wikis, graphs, mind maps and timelines, website ingestion through sitemaps, and Google BigQuery ingestion.

You can use the cloud service at cloud.ragflow.io or deploy it yourself with Docker Compose. After signing in, you add an LLM, an embedding model and a reranker on the model provider page. It also offers APIs for integrating with your business systems.

troubleshooting.solution: Set vm.max_map_count to at least 262144, and add it to /etc/sysctl.conf to keep it after reboots.
Inspect the logs with docker logs --tail 50 ragflow-cpu.
Wait until the health check returns HTTP 200; the container being up doesn't mean it's ready.
